images.title: One day out of 24 hours
images.purpose: Show that dividing a monthly daylight total by the days in the month gives daylight per day, which always fits inside 24 hours.
images.composition: Two long horizontal day strips, one above the other, centred with wide white margins; each has one short caption line above it.
exact_structure: Two identical horizontal strips, each the full length of a 24 hour day, marked 0 at the left end and 24 at the right end on a thin grey (#6B7280) scale under the lower strip.
Top strip: the left 18.8 of 24 parts (about 78 percent) filled amber (#E69F00) for daylight, the rest filled teal (#0072B2) for night.
Caption above the top strip: June: 564 ÷ 30 = 18.8 hours.
Bottom strip: the left 6 of 24 parts (one quarter) filled amber (#E69F00), the rest teal (#0072B2).
Caption above the bottom strip: December: 186 ÷ 31 = 6 hours.
A small key at the right: an amber square labelled daylight and a teal square labelled night.
rejection: the amber part of the June strip not about three quarters long
the amber part of the December strip not one quarter long
images.takeaway: Daylight per day is the monthly total divided by the days in that month, and it never passes 24 hours.
images.description: Two day strips from 0 to 24 hours: June with 18.8 hours of amber daylight, December with 6 hours.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Have students check each division and see the amber part never runs past 24.

image_decisions.why: A day strip makes the meaning of a daily average and the 24 hour limit visible.
